title: Steve Jobs Paid $10 Million For A Hobby And Got $7 Billion

beats.say: In 1986, Steve Jobs paid about ten million dollars for a small computer graphics company nobody wanted.
beats.visual: a dim empty workshop with an old computer under a single hanging lamp, no people

beats.say: It was Pixar, a unit Lucasfilm was selling. Jobs paid five million for it and put in about five million more.
beats.visual: two steel keys resting on a dark wooden desk beside a stack of blueprints, warm lamp light, no people

beats.say: For years it lost money, and plenty of people called it an expensive hobby.
beats.visual: a dusty drafting desk covered in crumpled paper balls under one lamp at night, no people

beats.say: Then in nineteen ninety five, Toy Story arrived, and Pixar went public.
beats.visual: a bright projector beam cutting through dark theatre dust toward a blank screen, no people

beats.say: Jobs owned most of the company, and the value of his shares took off.
beats.visual: a tall tower of gold coins rising into a dark sky, dramatic low angle

beats.say: So what happened to that ten million dollar bet?
beats.visual: a single brass key lying alone on a black table, hard rim light

beats.say: In two thousand six, Disney bought Pixar for about seven point four billion dollars, paid in Disney stock.
beats.visual: a grand marble staircase inside an empty film studio lobby at sunrise, no people

beats.say: Jobs held about half of Pixar, so he became Disney's largest individual shareholder.
beats.visual: a long empty boardroom table with one chair pulled out, golden window light, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. He did not get rich by being paid. He got rich by owning.
beats.visual: two hands passing a heavy brass key across a dark table, close-up, no faces

beats.say: A salary stops when the work stops. Ownership can keep growing while you sleep.
beats.visual: a quiet city skyline at night with a few lit windows, wide shot, no people

beats.say: The honest catch: Pixar lost money for years, and the payoff took about twenty years to arrive.
beats.visual: a stormy sea with waves rising under a heavy sky and a lighthouse in the distance

beats.say: Most bets like this do not work out, so owning a piece is a risk, not a promise.
beats.visual: a narrow rope bridge crossing a foggy canyon at dawn, no people

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: Jobs paid about $10M for Pixar in 1986. Disney paid about $7.4B in stock in 2006. Ownership vs salary, and the catch. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: In 1986 Steve Jobs bought Pixar for about ten million dollars in total; Disney bought it in 2006 for about 7.4 billion dollars in stock. What ownership did that a salary could not, and the honest catch.
first_comment: Would you take a salary or a piece of the company? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: 1986: Jobs bought Pixar's graphics unit from Lucasfilm for $5M and invested about $5M more
facts.basis: Walter Isaacson, Steve Jobs (2011); Pixar corporate history

facts.claim: Pixar went public in Nov 1995 after Toy Story; Jobs held a majority stake
facts.basis: SEC S-1 / Pixar IPO coverage, Nov 1995

facts.claim: Disney acquired Pixar in 2006 for about $7.4B in stock
Jobs became Disney's largest individual shareholder (about 7%)
Catch: Pixar lost money for years before Toy Story
